attempts.summary: Used Ansible from node2 (the only node with ansible-core installed and a pre-provisioned root SSH key, i.e. the configured control node) to harden node1's /tmp and /dev/shm mounts with noexec,nosuid,nodev via the ansible.posix.mount module, persisted through /etc/fstab. Verified live enforcement (execution, setuid privilege escalation, and device-node access all blocked) both before and after a full reboot of node1. Also completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart-evidence protocol on node2 (the control node), confirming its Ansible tooling and connectivity to node1 survived the restart and that a post-reboot playbook re-run is fully idempotent (changed=0).
